title: Fish Tacos with Lime Slaw
description: Smoky spice-rubbed white fish, flaked into warm corn tortillas with a sharp lime and coriander slaw, avocado and a cooling soured cream sauce.

steps.text: Juice the two slaw limes and set aside 1 tbsp of the juice for the crema. Put the cabbage in a large bowl with the lime zest, the rest of the juice, the salt and sugar. Scrunch hard with your hands for a minute until it starts to soften and turn bright pink, then leave to sit.
Stir the soured cream, mayonnaise, hot sauce and reserved lime juice together in a small bowl. Taste and add more hot sauce if you like.

Pat the fish very dry with kitchen paper and cut into strips about 3 cm wide. Mix the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder, garlic powder and salt, then turn the fish gently in the spices and 1 tbsp of the oil until evenly coated.

Heat the remaining oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Lay in the fish and cook without moving it until the underside is browned, about 3 minutes, then turn carefully and cook for 2 minutes more, until opaque all the way through and just starting to flake.
steps.tip: Cook in two batches if the pan is crowded, otherwise the fish steams and will not take on colour.

steps.text: Warm the tortillas one or two at a time in a dry frying pan over a high heat for about 30 seconds a side, until soft and lightly toasted in spots. Stack them in a clean tea towel to keep warm.
Stir the spring onions and coriander through the slaw. Fill each tortilla with slaw, a few pieces of fish and some avocado, spoon over the crema and serve with lime wedges.

tips: Corn tortillas crack if they are not properly warmed. Heat them just before serving and keep them wrapped.
Choose thick fillets where you can. Thin tail pieces cook in half the time and break up easily.

substitutions.note: cook for 1–2 minutes a side until pink

storage: Best eaten fresh. The slaw, without the herbs, and the crema both keep for 2 days in the fridge; cooked fish keeps for 1 day and is good cold.
author: Simmer
